This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts cancellation loop aborts on null referenceId: query lacks referenceId not-null filter, sends batch_id: null to SendGrid causing 400 that exits the loop and blocks cancellation of all subsequent reminders

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation query selects reminders with `{ cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` but does not filter `referenceId` to be non-null. The subsequent loop always calls SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`; if `referenceId` is `null`, this will likely cause the request to throw. Because the entire loop is wrapped in a single `try { for (...) { await client.request(...) ... } } catch { ... }`, the first such error aborts the loop and prevents cancellation/deletion of later reminders. The diff elsewhere (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId: string | null, ...)`) indicates `referenceId` can indeed be null, making this a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Serialized await SendGrid requests inside the for loop cause N sequential HTTP round-trips that can exceed cron timeout with a backlog

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block iterates `remindersToCancel` and does `await client.request(...)` inside a `for (const reminder ...)` loop, which serializes the SendGrid HTTP cancellations (one round-trip at a time). Only the Prisma deletes are batched via `Promise.all` after the loop. This diff-grounded pattern can create significant latency with many reminders and risks exceeding an API/cron execution time budget under backlog, but it’s primarily a performance/robustness concern rather than a definite functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts ~line 964: async forEach with floating promises; try/catch cannot catch async errors, and if workflowReminders is undefined (include only added to one query) the forEach throws synchronously and is swallowed, so no old reminders are cancelled on reschedule
handleCancelBooking.ts and bookings.tsx: cancellation promises fired without await; request may return before completion and serverless functions killed mid-flight, leaving reminders active

adjudication.rationale: In both `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, the diff changes reminder cancellation to call `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` without `await` and without collecting the returned promises. In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the prior `remindersToDelete` Prisma promises were removed and `prismaPromises` no longer includes any reminder-cancellation work, so `await Promise.all(...)` will not wait for these async cancellations. In `bookings.tsx`, it similarly removed `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` and now just fires async deletes in a `forEach`. This can allow the handler to complete before cancellations/deletions finish, risking reminders remaining scheduled/existing if the process terminates early.

adjudication_records.issue_text: emailReminderManager.ts non-immediate path only sets cancelled: true in DB and relies on cron to cancel at SendGrid within the final hour; cron outage means emails sent for cancelled bookings

adjudication.rationale: In the new `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` implementation, the non-`immediateDelete` path does not cancel the SendGrid scheduled send; it only sets `cancelled: true` in the DB (`prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })`). Call sites like `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, and parts of `viewer/workflows.tsx` invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, so the SendGrid job remains active. Actual cancellation at SendGrid is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only processes `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. Therefore, if that API/cron doesn't run in the final hour (or runs late), the SendGrid emails can still be sent for cancelled/rescheduled bookings—this incorrect behavior is directly implied by the diff's logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.workflowReminder.update failure in emailReminderManager is swallowed by console.log so the cancelled flag can fail to persist with no alert

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder()` now relies on `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true }})` to persist cancellation when `referenceId` exists and `immediateDelete` is falsy. That whole path is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and does not rethrow/propagate errors. If the `update` fails, the function resolves successfully, so callers get no signal and the `cancelled` flag may not be set, which can prevent later cancellation logic (e.g. `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` querying `cancelled: true`) from ever running for that reminder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: emailReminderManager.ts: all error modes including P2025 collapse into console.log with no rethrow, so genuine failures to mark cancelled leave reminders on track to send silently

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` wraps all paths in a broad `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and does not rethrow/propagate failure. With the new behavior for the common case (`referenceId` present, `immediateDelete` falsy) it *only* does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true }})` and does not cancel the external scheduled send immediately. If that update fails (including Prisma errors like record-not-found), the error is swallowed and the reminder remains not-cancelled and can still be sent, with no signal to callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx ~line 372: auth scoping removed — deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes/updates by id alone without owner check, allowing mutation of other users' reminders

adjudication.rationale: In workflows.tsx the previous guarded deletion used `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` but the new code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` which (per the diff) perform `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` with no owner/user scoping. From the diff we can’t confirm an actual auth bypass (the `reminder` objects may already be selected in a user-scoped query), but the change clearly removes a defense-in-depth authorization constraint at the mutation point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx disabled-workflow email reminders only flagged cancelled and persist indefinitely in DB since cron only deletes them within the 1-hour window

adjudication.rationale: In `workflows.tsx`, disabling workflows now calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, which in `emailReminderManager.ts` only sets `cancelled: true` (does not delete immediately). However, the diff also adds cleanup logic in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that finds `WorkflowReminder` rows with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`, cancels them via the provider API, and then deletes them from the DB. So the reminders are not shown to “persist indefinitely”; they persist until they fall within the cron’s 1-hour cancellation window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflows.tsx ~line 569: remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) floating promises; non-immediate email path can leave old scheduled reminders active while new ones are scheduled, sending both old and new reminders

adjudication.rationale: In `workflows.tsx` around the referenced block, the code uses `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... })` but does not `await` the async cancellation calls (and `forEach` won’t be awaited anyway). This creates floating promises for both `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`, so the mutation can proceed to later logic (e.g., updating steps/scheduling new reminders) before the old reminders are actually marked cancelled/deleted. That race can lead to duplicate/old reminders remaining active long enough to be scheduled/sent alongside new ones (especially on the email path where the non-`immediateDelete` branch only updates `cancelled: true`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts reschedule: un-awaited cancel can race with scheduling new reminders for the replacement booking, and failures are silent

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new cancellation logic calls async functions inside `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` without awaiting them (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`). `forEach` does not await promises, so cancellation can run concurrently with subsequent reschedule/scheduling logic. Also, the surrounding `try/catch` will not catch async rejections from those un-awaited calls, making failures effectively silent/unhandled despite the log intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts: cancelled reminders with past scheduledDate are only deleted if SendGrid cancel succeeds; on error rows accumulate forever and cancels are retried eternally

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts, cancelled reminders are fetched (cancelled: true, scheduledDate <= now+1h), then inside a single try/catch each reminder is first cancelled via SendGrid (client.request) and only afterwards a prisma.workflowReminder.delete() promise is queued. If any SendGrid cancel throws, control jumps to the catch and the DB delete(s) are not awaited/executed for the remaining (and possibly already-queued) reminders, leaving rows with cancelled=true in the table. Those rows will be selected again on every run, causing repeated retries and potential indefinite accumulation when SendGrid cancellation keeps failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded findMany query for cancelled reminders with no take/pagination in cron handler

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic does `prisma.workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() }}})` with no `take`/pagination (and no batching). This is a real, diff-grounded scalability/performance concern for a cron-like handler: if many cancelled reminders accumulate with `scheduledDate` within the next hour, it will load and iterate over all of them in one run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SendGrid HTTP calls awaited serially inside a for loop, blocking cron for N × SendGrid latency

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop before collecting Prisma deletes for a later `Promise.all`. This makes the SendGrid cancellation HTTP requests run sequentially (N× network latency), which can unnecessarily slow/block the cron/API handler even though the subsequent DB deletes are parallelized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single SendGrid error aborts the loop causing the whole batch to be re-fetched and re-cancelled on the next run, burning API quota

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cancellation loop is wrapped in a single `try` and performs `await client.request(...)` inside a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)`. If any one SendGrid request throws, control jumps to `catch` and the function never reaches `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`, so none of the DB deletes are awaited/executed. That leaves already-cancelled reminders still marked `cancelled: true` in the DB, so they will be re-fetched by the same `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... }}})` on the next run and re-cancelled again, potentially burning API quota.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New cancelled Boolean? column queried on every cron tick has no index, causing recurring table scans on large reminder tables

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `cancelled` column to `WorkflowReminder` (migration + `schema.prisma`) and introduces a periodic-looking query in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` that does `findMany` with `where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }`. The migration only adds the column and does not add any index, and the Prisma schema does not declare an `@@index` on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate`. This is a diff-grounded performance concern (potential recurring full scans as the table grows), not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Async deletion callbacks launched inside forEach without awaiting or collecting promises, so tRPC mutation returns before work completes and errors are swallowed silently
Fire-and-forget async loops in handleNewBooking.ts:964-972 and bookings.tsx:487-494 with no error visibility or retry orchestration

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces un-awaited async side effects in both places cited. In handleNewBooking.ts, within a try/catch, `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`, but those functions are `async` (see emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts) and are not awaited or collected into `Promise.all`. The surrounding try/catch will not catch async rejections, so failures become invisible and cancellation may not complete before the reschedule continues. Similarly in bookings.tsx, `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` calls the same async delete functions and the previous `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete);` was removed, making these cancellations fire-and-forget.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-reminder single-row DELETE queries replace the previously batched deleteMany, multiplying DB round-trips for bookings with many reminders

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce per-reminder single-row `delete` calls in places (e.g. `smsReminderManager.ts` now does `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id } })`, and `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` deletes each reminder by `id` in a loop). However, the removed logic was not actually a batched delete: it built an array of `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id } })`—still one DB query per reminder (just using `deleteMany` with a single `id`). So it’s not accurate to say this change “replaces previously batched deleteMany” or newly “multiplies” round-trips vs what was there; both versions are per-reminder operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: workflowReminders: true included eagerly on every new booking creation before knowing whether it's a reschedule, increasing payload on the hot path

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the Prisma include was expanded to `workflowReminders: true` (added alongside `payment: true`). This will fetch the full `workflowReminders` relation whenever that booking query runs, even though it’s only used later inside `if (originalRescheduledBooking?.uid) { ... originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...) }`. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded potential performance/payload concern (extra data loaded on the main request path), though the diff snippet doesn’t fully show whether this query executes for all new bookings or only when rescheduling.

Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags unawaited async reminder cancellation calls across booking reschedule/cancel and workflow-related code, leading to reminder deletions potentially not completing and users receiving email/SMS after cancellation. adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete=true path in emailReminderManager.ts cancels SendGrid batch but returns early without deleting or flag-canceling the DB row, leaving orphan rows with cancelled=false

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` returns early when `immediateDelete` is true after canceling the SendGrid batch (`/v3/user/scheduled_sends` POST) and does not `delete` or `update` the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row. Unlike the non-immediate path (which sets `cancelled: true`) or the `!referenceId` path (which deletes the row), this leaves the DB row intact with `cancelled` still unset/false. Call sites such as `handleNewBooking.ts` use `immediateDelete=true` for rescheduled bookings, and there is no accompanying DB cleanup in the diff, so this can leave stale/orphan reminder records and an inconsistent DB state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Useless try/catch around async forEach in handleNewBooking.ts cannot catch anything since promises are never awaited, making the error log dead code

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the new try/catch wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` (around line ~950). `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async (return promises), but they are invoked without `await`, and `forEach` does not await async work. Therefore any promise rejection would not be caught by the surrounding try/catch, and the handler will proceed without waiting for reminder cancellation/DB updates to complete, making the outer error log ineffective and potentially leaving cancellations incomplete in serverless/request-lifecycle contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email cancellation now relies on hourly cron window in scheduleEmailReminders.ts instead of immediate SendGrid cancellation, an implicit new SLA with no versioning/fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation behavior: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` no longer cancels SendGrid immediately by default; it only sets `cancelled: true` in Prisma (`emailReminderManager.ts`). Actual SendGrid cancellation now happens later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which periodically queries `workflowReminder` where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour` and then posts a SendGrid cancel request and deletes the record. Call sites like `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `viewer/bookings.tsx` use the non-`immediateDelete` path, so they rely on that later job. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/operational SLA change (depends on scheduleEmailReminders execution cadence) rather than a clearly provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If a SendGrid cancel fails mid-loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, Promise.all deletes are skipped for already-cancelled entries, leaving partially processed state on retry

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the cancellation+deletion logic is wrapped in a single `try { ... } catch { ... }`. Inside the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop, `await client.request(...)` can throw mid-iteration. If it throws, control jumps to `catch` and the function never reaches `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`, meaning any `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises already pushed are never awaited/executed. This leaves already-successfully-cancelled SendGrid entries still present in DB (`cancelled: true`) and they will be reprocessed on retry, creating a partially processed state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public function signature changes to deleteScheduledEmailReminder and SMS equivalent may break out-of-diff callers consuming the feature package; needs repo-wide grep

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the exported function signatures: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now requires `(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` (emailReminderManager.ts) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now requires `(reminderId, referenceId)` (smsReminderManager.ts). Multiple in-diff call sites were updated accordingly (handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts, viewer/bookings.tsx, viewer/workflows.tsx), but the diff cannot prove there are no remaining out-of-diff callers still using the old `(referenceId)` signature. A repo-wide grep/build check is warranted to avoid breaking any other consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rows with cancelled=true and null referenceId in scheduleEmailReminders.ts cron will send batch_id: null to SendGrid, throw, and block remaining loop iterations forever

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the loop does call SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` without a null-guard, but the diff’s own cancellation path (`deleteScheduledEmailReminder`) **deletes** reminders when `referenceId` is null and only sets `cancelled: true` when `referenceId` is truthy. So the specific scenario “cancelled=true and null referenceId” is not shown to be produced by this diff. Also, an exception would exit the `try` and skip remaining cancellations for that run, but it would not “block remaining loop iterations forever” (it just goes to `catch`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deferred cancellation lets reminder emails fire for cancelled bookings because SendGrid cancel is deferred to cron with 1-hour window

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes email reminder cancellation from immediate SendGrid cancellation to a deferred DB flag in most call sites. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` now (when `immediateDelete` is not passed) only does `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true }})` and does not call SendGrid cancel (emailReminderManager.ts). Actual SendGrid cancellation is moved to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only processes `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`. This creates a period where a cancelled booking’s reminder may still exist in SendGrid until the cron endpoint runs within that 1-hour window. Whether this actually "lets emails fire" depends on cron frequency/reliability (not shown in the diff), so it’s a concrete risk/edge-case introduced by the change rather than a strictly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Orphaned WorkflowReminder rows when immediateDelete is used: rows stay scheduled: true, cancelled: null and are never picked up by cron
Error in cancel loop aborts remaining cancellations with no per-reminder try/catch isolation, permanently blocking later cancellations

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation logic wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop in a single `try/catch`. Any thrown error from `client.request(...)` (or subsequent DB delete) will break out of the loop and skip cancelling/deleting the remaining reminders in `remindersToCancel`, meaning later reminders won’t be processed in that run. (Related: in `handleNewBooking.ts` a `try/catch` around a `forEach` that calls async `deleteScheduled*Reminder(...)` without `await` won’t isolate/catch per-reminder async failures either.) The finding’s “permanently blocking” wording is stronger than what the diff proves, but the “one error aborts remaining cancellations due to lack of per-item isolation” issue is directly evidenced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fire-and-forget reminder cancellation in forEach async callbacks is never awaited, causing races with response and reschedule flow

adjudication.rationale: In multiple places the diff calls newly-async cancellation functions inside `forEach` without awaiting or collecting the returned promises, so cancellation/DB updates can race with subsequent logic/response. Examples: `handleCancelBooking.ts` loops `updatedBookings.forEach(... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, ...) ...)` but `prismaPromises` no longer includes reminder operations; `handleNewBooking.ts` cancels reminders for `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` without `await`; `bookings.tsx` similarly; and `workflows.tsx` has `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` where the async callbacks are never awaited. Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now does `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete` and/or external cancel requests, not awaiting can leave reminders uncancelled when the handler proceeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead try/catch around non-awaited async forEach in handleNewBooking.ts:964-974 gives false error handling

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new try/catch wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` where it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`. Those functions are `async` (see emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts), but the calls are not awaited and `forEach` doesn’t propagate/await promises. As a result, the try/catch will not catch rejections from those async deletions, leading to false error handling and potential unhandled promise rejections / missed cancellation failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent failure modes: SMS reminders cancelled immediately while email reminders deferred to cron

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows different cancellation semantics by channel. `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` immediately calls `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` (if present) and then deletes the DB record (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete`). In contrast, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete?)` usually does not cancel the provider send; when `immediateDelete` is not passed it only marks the reminder as `cancelled: true` in DB (`prisma.workflowReminder.update`) and relies on `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` to later find `cancelled: true` reminders within the next hour, cancel them via `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`, and delete them. Many call sites (e.g. `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `viewer/bookings.tsx`, parts of `viewer/workflows.tsx`) call the email variant without `immediateDelete`, so emails are deferred to that periodic job while SMS is cancelled immediately. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency, but not provably a correctness defect without knowing intended behavior/cron guarantees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cancelled-but-far-future email reminders linger in DB until their 1-hour window, causing duplicate work and confusing scheduled: true, cancelled: true state

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes cancellation semantics for email reminders: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now (when `immediateDelete` is not passed) only marks the DB record `cancelled: true` via `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` and does not cancel the provider send or delete the row. Actual cancellation+deletion happens later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, but only for `cancelled: true` reminders whose `scheduledDate <= now+1 hour`. This means cancelled reminders scheduled farther in the future will remain in the DB for potentially a long time and can be in a mixed state (e.g., `scheduled: true` while `cancelled: true`), which is a legitimate consistency/clarity concern exposed by the diff. The claim about “duplicate work” isn’t directly demonstrated, but the lingering/confusing state is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EMAIL/SMS cancel-branch block is duplicated ~8 times across 5 files with inconsistent immediateDelete arguments; should be extracted into a single cancelWorkflowReminders helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same EMAIL/SMS branching logic repeated in multiple places (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts reschedule block, viewer/bookings.tsx reschedule, and several loops in viewer/workflows.tsx). Calls to deleteScheduledEmailReminder are sometimes made with immediateDelete=true (e.g., workflows.tsx deleted workflow/step, handleNewBooking.ts) and sometimes without it (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts, viewer/bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx disable event types / edited steps). Since immediateDelete changes behavior in emailReminderManager (either cancels immediately vs marking cancelled=true), the duplication plus differing arguments is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/consistency concern; however the diff alone doesn’t prove any specific call site is incorrect, so it’s not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete=true path in emailReminderManager.ts cancels the SendGrid batch but never deletes, cancels, or updates the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaving it permanently stale (scheduled: true, cancelled: null) and accumulating zombie rows

adjudication.rationale:
In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId, immediateDelete)` does:
- if `!referenceId`: deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row.
- if `immediateDelete`: cancels the SendGrid batch via POST `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` and then `return;` without deleting or updating the `WorkflowReminder` row.
- else: updates the row to `{ cancelled: true }`.
So the `immediateDelete=true` path leaves the DB row untouched (no `cancelled` flag, no delete). Call sites in the diff use `immediateDelete=true` (e.g. `workflowsRouter` when deleting workflow/steps), meaning reminders can remain as stale/zombie rows and also won’t be cleaned up by the new `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` logic since that cleanup queries `cancelled: true` only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The three persistence outcomes (referenceId null → delete row, immediateDelete → cancel send only, default → mark cancelled but don't delete) are inconsistent and undocumented

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` has three divergent DB outcomes: (1) `referenceId` null -> hard delete `workflowReminder` row (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete`), (2) `immediateDelete` true -> cancels send via API then `return` without deleting or marking `cancelled`, (3) default -> only updates row `cancelled: true` without cancelling immediately. This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded (emailReminderManager.ts). It’s also asymmetric with SMS which always deletes the row after optional cancel. Whether it’s a “bug” isn’t provable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete behavioral/maintenance concern and can leave email reminder rows behind with no follow-up deletion path shown for the `immediateDelete` case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scheduleEmailReminders.ts reimplements cancellation with raw SendGrid calls and its own prisma.workflowReminder.delete instead of calling emailReminderManager.ts, coupling the cron route to the SendGrid wire protocol and causing the implementations to diverge

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block directly calls the SendGrid scheduled_sends endpoint via `client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` and then deletes reminders with `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`, instead of reusing the centralized `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` in `emailReminderManager.ts` (which now encapsulates cancellation/DB behavior and has an `immediateDelete` option). This duplicates/couples the cron route to the SendGrid wire protocol and creates two cancellation implementations that can diverge (they already differ: manager marks `cancelled=true` vs cron cancels+deletes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts, await client.request(...) inside a for loop serializes API calls

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the new cancellation block iterates `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` and does `await client.request(...)` inside the loop before collecting Prisma deletes. This makes the external API cancellation requests run sequentially rather than concurrently, which can unnecessarily slow the handler when many reminders need canceling. It’s a performance/scalability concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the array-of-Promise-values pattern (workflowRemindersToDelete built from already-invoked prisma queries) is a footgun

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts the code builds an array of Prisma delete operations (`prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id } })`) and awaits them via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. This is a standard pattern: the Prisma calls return thenables/promises that are executed when awaited/consumed by Promise.all, and nothing in the diff shows these queries are being “already-invoked” in a problematic way or causing incorrect behavior. The try/catch also wraps the whole block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Try-catch around async forEach in handleNewBooking.ts can never catch anything because the manager functions swallow their own errors and the promises aren't awaited, making it dead code giving false safety

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new block wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` in a `try/catch`, but the callbacks invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` without `await`. Any async rejection would not be caught by this `try/catch` because the promises are not awaited. Additionally, both manager functions shown in the diff (`emailReminderManager.deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `smsReminderManager.deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) already catch and log errors internally and do not rethrow, so the outer `try/catch` is effectively misleading/ineffective error handling (false sense of safety) rather than providing real protection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: At workflows.tsx:575-583, remindersToUpdate.forEach(async ...) fires and forgets before the mutation returns (unawaited async forEach pattern)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff shows `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` and inside it calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)`, which are `async` functions (per their definitions in `emailReminderManager.ts` and `smsReminderManager.ts`). `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await the async callbacks, and there is no surrounding `await Promise.all(...)` or other awaiting of the returned promises. As a result, reminder cancellations/deletes can still be in-flight after the mutation continues/returns (fire-and-forget). This is a real behavioral defect exposed by the change, especially since the prior `await ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` inside the loop was removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isSenderIdNeeded was silently dropped from the render condition in WorkflowStepContainer.tsx, either leaving dead code or making an undocumented behavior change bundled into a reminder-lifecycle PR (separation-of-concerns violation)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `WorkflowStepContainer.tsx` changes the render guard from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to only `isPhoneNumberNeeded`, so any UI that previously appeared when `isSenderIdNeeded` was true (but `isPhoneNumberNeeded` was false) will no longer render. The diff also shows no replacement UI handling for `isSenderIdNeeded` inside that block, implying either an undocumented behavior change or dead/unused `isSenderIdNeeded` logic elsewhere. This is a concrete, diff-grounded scope/behavior concern, though the diff alone can’t prove it breaks a real user flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace/indentation corruption in workflows.tsx ~lines 901+ including leftover commented-out code, polluting blame/diff history and suggesting a broken paste

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx` around the shown ~901+ region, the diff clearly introduces large-scale indentation/whitespace changes (many lines lose their leading spaces) and retains odd commented-out fragments in the `if (isSMSAction(step.action) /*|| ...*/ /*) {` line. This is diff/noise and maintainability/blame pollution grounded in the patch, rather than a clearly demonstrated runtime defect from the snippet alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cancellation promises in handleCancelBooking.ts and bookings.tsx are never awaited; reminder deletions race with Promise.all and the transaction, and failures are silently lost since the functions swallow errors internally

adjudication.rationale: In both `handleCancelBooking.ts` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`, the code now calls async `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `forEach` without `await` or collecting the returned promises. The prior Prisma deletion promises (`remindersToDelete` + `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)`) were removed, so reminder cancellation/deletion is no longer synchronized with the surrounding `Promise.all(...)` (and thus can race/continue after the main operation). Additionally, both reminder-manager functions catch and only `console.log` errors, so failures are effectively dropped and won’t fail the outer flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cancelled Boolean? in schema.prisma is nullable with tri-state semantics where null, false, and true are all possible but only true is ever queried and false is never written; should be non-null default false to avoid null-vs-false confusion in queries
matched_golden_ids: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the `cancelled` field is nullable, leading to possible `null` values instead of a default `false`, which can cause incorrect behavior/confusion when checking cancellation status. Candidate additionally mentions tri-state semantics and recommends non-null with default false, aligning with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron cancellation loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts crashes on reminders with null referenceId, causing the outer try/catch to skip all DB deletes and permanently wedge the cron

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation block selects cancelled reminders without filtering out `referenceId: null`, then unconditionally calls the email provider with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId` inside a single outer `try { ... } catch { ... }`. If any reminder has `referenceId === null`, that request can throw and the catch will skip the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` pushes/`Promise.all`, leaving those reminders undeleted and causing the same cancellation block to fail again on future runs. The diff shows no null-guard here (unlike `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, which explicitly handles `!referenceId`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminder cancellation calls in handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts, and viewer/bookings.tsx are fire-and-forget (never awaited), so cancellations may never execute in serverless contexts

adjudication.rationale: In all three spots, the code invokes async cancellation helpers inside `forEach` without `await` (e.g., `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `handleNewBooking.ts`, and `viewer/bookings.tsx`). The diff also removed the prior `PrismaPromise` collection + `Promise.all(...)` that ensured reminder deletions completed. This makes reminder cancellations effectively fire-and-forget and can lead to cancellations/deletes not completing before the handler returns (a real risk in serverless/request lifecycles).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In handleNewBooking.ts the try/catch around the forEach cannot catch async rejections, making the error log dead code and leaving rejections unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the new block wraps `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` in a try/catch, but the calls are to `async` functions and their returned Promises are neither `await`ed nor collected. As written, the outer try/catch cannot catch promise rejections from those async operations, so it does not provide the intended error handling. However, in this diff both `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` include their own internal try/catch and swallow/log errors, so the claim about “leaving rejections unhandled” isn’t clearly a concrete defect here; it’s still a specific, diff-grounded robustness issue (misleading/error-handling that won’t work if the callee ever rejects).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SMS reminder rows are not deleted if Twilio cancelSMS throws, and there is no retry path for SMS reminders, leaving a scheduled SMS live with no recovery mechanism

adjudication.rationale: In smsReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId) wraps both `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `await prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` in a single try/catch. If `twilio.cancelSMS` throws, the DB delete is skipped and only logged, leaving the WorkflowReminder row intact. The diff also removed the previous external `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` cleanup in callers (e.g., handleCancelBooking.ts, bookings router, workflows router), so there is no longer a guaranteed DB deletion or alternate retry/cancellation path for SMS (unlike email, which now can mark `cancelled` and later cancel via scheduleEmailReminders).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SMS cancellation failures are silently swallowed by the catch which only logs

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` wraps both `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and the Prisma delete in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and does not rethrow/propagate errors. As a result, callers (which in multiple places invoke it without `await`) cannot detect or handle SMS cancellation failures beyond logs. This is a concrete, diff-grounded error-handling concern, but not a verifiable functional defect on its own because the intended behavior on cancellation failure is not specified in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete path in emailReminderManager.ts cancels at SendGrid but never updates or deletes the DB row, leaving orphaned rows that look active (especially in the reschedule path)
Ownership check dropped in workflows.tsx: deleteScheduledSMSReminder/deleteScheduledEmailReminder delete by bare id with no user ownership scoping, allowing potential cross-user deletion

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, several call sites replaced `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` with `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, ...)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)`. The new helpers (`emailReminderManager.ts` / `smsReminderManager.ts`) perform `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` using a global `prisma` client and do not include any `booking.userId`/ownership constraint. This is a concrete drop of DB-level ownership scoping compared to the previous code and can enable cross-user reminder cancellation/deletion if an attacker can cause another user's `reminder.id` to be targeted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: async callback inside forEach in workflows.tsx reminder update is fire-and-forget: cancellations race with subsequent DB writes and failures are unhandled while the route returns success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, the diff shows `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); ... deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); });` where the async callback (and the async cancellation functions it calls) are not awaited or collected into `Promise.all`. This makes reminder cancellations fire-and-forget: failures are not propagated/handled and subsequent logic/DB writes can proceed (and the route can return success) before cancellations complete, creating a real race condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email reminders for cancelled bookings can still be sent due to cancel-at-send-time race: soft cancellation only sets cancelled flag in DB and defers SendGrid cancellation to cron, which only handles reminders within 1 hour window

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes cancellation behavior for email workflow reminders: most call sites now invoke `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` without `immediateDelete`, which in `emailReminderManager.ts` no longer cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but only sets `cancelled: true` in the DB (`prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)`). Actual SendGrid cancellation is deferred to `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, which only looks for `cancelled: true` reminders with `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour` and then issues the SendGrid cancel call. This introduces a design dependency on the cron/API job running reliably/frequently enough before send time; otherwise a scheduled send could still fire. The diff alone doesn’t prove reminders will “still be sent” (cron frequency/guarantees aren’t shown), but it does show the deferred-cancel + 1-hour window mechanism that creates this potential race/reliability concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent cancellation behavior between email (deferred to cron) and SMS (cancelled immediately)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly makes email reminder cancellation potentially deferred while SMS is cancelled/deleted immediately. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now only marks the DB row as `cancelled: true` unless `immediateDelete` is passed (or `referenceId` is null), and actual provider cancellation/deletion is handled later in `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` for reminders within the next hour. By contrast, `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` calls `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` (if present) and then deletes the `workflowReminder` record right away. This is an inconsistency in behavior introduced/relied upon by the new code paths (e.g., booking cancel/reschedule uses deferred email cancellation but immediate SMS cancellation). Whether it’s intended or not isn’t provable from the diff alone, but the inconsistency is real and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cron cancellation loop in scheduleEmailReminders.ts doesn't filter out reminders with null referenceId, causing SendGrid to throw on batch_id: null and abort the entire loop, leaving remaining reminders uncanceled and undeleted

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new cancellation loop queries `workflowReminder.findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { ... }}})` without filtering for non-null `referenceId`, then calls SendGrid with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`. The diff elsewhere shows `referenceId` can be `string | null` (e.g. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, referenceId: string | null, ...)`). If any cancelled reminder has `referenceId === null`, this code will send `batch_id: null` and likely throw; because the entire loop is wrapped in a single `try/catch`, one failure aborts cancelling/deleting the remaining reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single SendGrid failure in the cron cancellation loop poisons the rest of the batch so remaining reminders are neither cancelled nor deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, the new “cancel reminders” logic wraps the entire cancellation loop in a single `try { ... } catch { ... }` (lines added around the `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...) ... }`). If SendGrid `client.request` throws for any one reminder, control jumps to the outer `catch`, and the loop stops, so subsequent reminders are not cancelled and their DB deletes are never queued/awaited. This matches the finding that one failure poisons the rest of the batch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: immediateDelete path cancels SendGrid but returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder DB row, leaving orphaned scheduled:true, cancelled:null rows that accumulate and may be re-processed
matched_golden_ids: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: when `immediateDelete` is true, the function exits after handling SendGrid without removing/updating the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row, leaving orphaned records that can accumulate/reprocess. While it doesn’t explicitly mention the missing SendGrid DELETE API call, it matches the primary database-orphan/inconsistent behavior issue described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reminders with cancelled:true flag may not be filtered out of scheduling/send queries (unscheduledReminders, sendScheduledEmails cron), risking cancelled booking reminders being (re)scheduled or sent

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `WorkflowReminder.cancelled` flag and changes `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` to mark reminders as `cancelled: true` (when not `immediateDelete`) instead of deleting them (`emailReminderManager.ts`). In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts`, cancellation processing only targets reminders where `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1h`, but the subsequent "find all unscheduled Email reminders" query is not updated in this diff to exclude `cancelled` reminders (no added `cancelled: false/null` condition). This makes it plausible that cancelled reminders (especially those outside the 1-hour window) could still be picked up by existing scheduling/sending queries and be (re)scheduled/sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reschedule path (bookings.tsx, handleCancelBooking.tsx) fires deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder promises via forEach without awaiting, risking old reminders not cancelled while new ones scheduled, causing duplicate reminders

adjudication.rationale: In both reschedule/cancel paths the diff invokes async cancellation functions inside `forEach` without awaiting them. E.g. `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...)` inside `workflowReminders.forEach` and no longer has any `Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` afterward. Similarly in `handleCancelBooking.ts` the reminders are no longer deleted/awaited (removed `remindersToDelete` and removed them from `prismaPromises`), but still call the async delete/cancel functions without awaiting. Since `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` now performs DB writes (`prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete`) and sometimes external cancellation, not awaiting can race with subsequent scheduling and/or let the handler finish before cancellations persist, risking duplicate reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ownership scoping removed from reminder deletion: old deleteMany filtered by booking userId, new deletion in reminder managers has no user scoping, risking deleting other users' reminders if future callers pass unscoped IDs

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes explicit ownership scoping on reminder DB deletion in at least one place: previously `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` (in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`) enforced user ownership, but the new flow calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` which in the managers performs `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId }})` (SMS) or `prisma.workflowReminder.update/delete` by `id` (Email) with no user/booking scoping. Current call sites appear to pass reminder objects already fetched in context, so this isn’t a clearly exploitable bug from the diff alone, but it does reduce defense-in-depth and creates a risk if any caller ever provides an unscoped/attacker-controlled reminder id.
